title: refactor(ci): consolidate workflows, optimize lint/test/release & cache hygiene
author: Ava Thompson
description:
Motivation: The repo currently has multiple narrowly-scoped GitHub workflows (lint.yml, test.yml, release.yml, build.yml) with duplicated setup steps, inconsistent caching strategies, and outdated action versions. This causes longer CI time, cache misses, and maintenance overhead when updating CI defaults (Node versions, checkout/setup-node, actions/cache usage).

Summary of changes: Consolidate lint/test/release pipelines into a single .github/workflows/ci.yml that uses job matrices and path filters; standardize on Node 20 across JS/TS jobs; bump common GH Action versions (actions/checkout v4, actions/setup-node v4, pnpm/action-setup v2); introduce centralized cache helper composite action to ensure consistent restore/keys across packages; add conditional test splitting to parallelize slow integration/e2e tests on self-hosted runners; introduce concurrency groups and path-based workflow triggers to reduce redundant runs on documentation/markdown changes.

Checklist: 
- [x] Consolidated workflows into ci.yml with matrix for node versions and package groups
- [x] Standardized action versions & cache keys (restore-keys improved to reduce miss rate)
- [x] Split long-running e2e/integration into parallelized jobs with retry-on-flake
- [x] Preserved release automation semantics (tag triggers, changelog generation)
- [x] Updated docs: tools/ci/README.md explaining new workflow layout and recommended contributor guidance

Testing and rollout: I iterated on this branch to fix an initial e2e flake (see CI history). All checks passed after two reruns. We gated the release job to manual approval for the first week after rollout and kept the old release.yml as a disabled historical file for 72 hours to help any in-flight ops. After monitoring, the historical file was removed in a follow-up commit.

Notes: This PR does not alter runtime code or production infra. It is focused on developer workflow hygiene and CI performance. The change reduces total CI cost by consolidating duplicate work and improves median CI wall time for PRs touching multiple packages by ~20% in our test runs. See ENG-1874 for perf measurements and ENG-1920 for rollout plan.
commits: chore(ci): add consolidated .github/workflows/ci.yml and composite cache helper
fix(ci): tweak e2e retry/backoff to avoid transient failures
chore(actions): bump actions/checkout to v4 and actions/setup-node to v4
perf(ci): split integration tests into parallel matrix on self-hosted runners
docs(ci): update tools/ci/README.md and contributor guidance
review_comments: Jordan Lee: This looks like a great consolidation — a couple of asks: (1) can we make the cache keys deterministic across monorepo packages, (2) please add a short note about why Node 20 was chosen and the compatibility matrix with older runtimes.

Ava Thompson: Reply: added centralized cache-helper composite action and added a note in README explaining Node 20 selection (LTS + toolchain support). Updated cache keys to include package name + lockfile hash for stability.
Priya Desai: Nit: prefer actions/checkout@v4 with fetch-depth: 0 for monorepo-aware test tooling — can you add that?
Ava Thompson: Done — changed checkout step to fetch-depth: 0 and re-ran the full CI. Added comment in workflow about why shallow clones break some tools.
Marcus Chen: Approve after addressing retry/backoff for e2e flake. LGTM.
CI Bot: e2e job failed on first run (timeout). Rerun triggered. Second run passed. All checks green.
release_notes: Consolidated CI workflows into a single ci.yml; standardized Node to v20; improved caching strategy and parallelized long-running tests. No production behavior changes. Expected shorter PR CI times and lower CI costs.
